watches.name: Experimental: ARC II — Poltergeist
watches.description: A Restrained Spirit Even our wild side occasionally wears a clean shirt. The ARC II — Poltergeist brings our appetite for unusual materials together with a distinctly Scandinavian sense of restraint. We’ve kept the palette deliberately quiet, allowing the interplay between materials and textures to create the contrast. The irregular structure of aerospace-grade aluminium foam sits against the clean lines of a rhodium-plated chapter ring and matching hands. The micro-blasted steel case adds a softer texture of its own. Across this narrow spectrum of whites and silvers, each surface responds differently to the light. Of course, restraint has its limits. After dark, a powerful X1 white lume developed by our Swiss friends at RC Tritec shines through the resin-filled aluminium foam, bringing its irregular structure into sharp relief. At the center, a white lume-filled rhodium-plated triple handset (hours, minutes, and seconds) in the Grand Paw style, improving legibility against the irregular distribution of the aluminium foam. Available in our original 40.5 mm case and the new 37 mm size, the Poltergeist brings a quieter expression to the Experimental collection. Even though poltergeists are the loudest of ghosts, ours is probably the quietest spirit we’ve conjured in a long while. This is a time-limited release, debuting on October 31st, 2026, and crossing over to the astral plane on November 30th, at midnight CET. The Arc II — Poltergeist can be ordered now either via Arcanaut's website or via selected official retailers .

The inimitable testaments to time you see before you, is handcrafted by Arcanaut co-owner James Thompson (AKA Black Badger) in his workshop in Gothenburg, Sweden. watches.name: Experimental: ARC II — Chronomara
watches.description: The Arc II — Chronomara brings Irish Connemara marble to life with a luminous composite dial, handcrafted in Copenhagen. Created in honour of independent watchmaking champion Johnny McElherron, it combines Irish heritage with Scandinavian experimentation. We crush the marble and transform it into a semi-translucent hand polished composite, preserving its rich green character. Layered above solid Lumicast and beneath a sapphire disc, the dial reveals depth by day and an intense characterful glow after dark. It marks the debut of our new four-layer dial construction, opening new possibilities for combining natural materials and light. Limited to 66 individually numbered pieces across 37 mm and 40.5 mm sizes.

watches.name: Black Badger UV Torch
watches.description: A proper little tool for anyone who enjoys seeing lume do what lume is supposed to do. Designed by our good friend James Thompson, better known as Black Badger , co-owner of Arcanaut and long-time master of luminous mischief, this UV torch is made to quickly charge and show off Super-LumiNova in all its glowing glory. The UV light emits at a 365nm wavelength which is the sweet spot for activating photoluminescent materials. Ideal for Arcanaut watches, Black Badger rings, and other luminous objects, it is compact, robust, and easy to keep close at hand. A practical companion for collectors, enthusiasts, and anyone with a healthy appreciation for things that glow in the dark. Please note: Batteries are not included due to international shipping restrictions. The Black Badger UV Torch uses a rechargeable 18650 lithium-ion battery (3.7V, 2600mAh) .

watches.name: Arc II – D'Arc Sh'Arc: Astax Pink
watches.description: The Arc II - D'Arc Sh'Arc: Astax Pink is what happens when brutal Nordic slate stone collides with pink Miami neon. The result? A wrist-sized anomaly that glows like a reactor core in the dark. Experiment Log: #DS-AP We wanted to see how far pink lume could go, so we went to RC Tritec and asked for something that didn't exist. The result is Astax Pink, the strongest glowing pink lume ever made (according to Tritec and our moms). Under the sapphire crystal, coated with a colour-matched pink anti-reflective coating, the lume hums softly against the raw grey-black dial; under darkness, it detonates into a vibrant halo that borders on radioactive. The dial itself is made from pulverized Scandinavian slate, cast and milled, with a cratered texture we call D'Arc Matter. The case is crafted from a zirconium-titanium composite, which is tailor-made for Arcanaut by Nichols Damascus in the USA. The material reveals hypnotic dark-grey striations when heat-treated to an exact temperature. Each one is bead-blasted to accentuate the layered texture, creating a matte finish that feels stealthy, sharp, and organic. The Astax Pink is limited to only 15 pieces.

watches.name: Experimental: ARC II — Phantom
watches.description: The Arcanaut ARC II – Phantom Born of shadow and subtle menace, the Phantom is a darker, more elusive sibling in our Experimentals collection. The Experimentals collection debuted in 2023 with the announcement of the Bonehead and Tiger Sh'Arc pieces which quickly sold out. In late 2024, these ambitious designs finally landed on the wrists of their new owners. Born of shadow and subtle menace, the Phantom is a darker, more elusive sibling in our Experimentals collection. The Phantom revisits the complex, multi-layered dial construction first seen in the Bonehead. A solid disc of Super-LumiNova sits beneath a resin-injected layer of aerospace-grade aluminium foam, topped by a German Silver chapter ring — now re-engineered as a structural “carrier” for both lume and foam. This time, the SLN disc glows with an enigmatic violet hue. The hands are now PVD-coated in a custom-mixed purple tone, perfectly matched to the dial. The chapter ring is blasted silver German Silver, subtly updated for improved construction, with a sleek black strap grounding the colourway. On the back you’ll find one of our signature GlowPatch style casebacks, hand-infilled with Super-Luminova and protected behind a sapphire crystal, now in the style of cowled phantom. Limited to just 66 pieces, the Phantom shares its skeletonized case with our other experimental pieces, machined and finished in Denmark, with hands, dial and caseback made in our workshop in Copenhagen. Questions? Reach out to Rob at rob@arcanaut.dk

watches.name: Experimental: ARC II — Garnet Goblin
watches.description: What’s the story? The GPHG-nominated Arcanaut ARC II – Garnet Goblin is a surface-dwelling stunner born of fire, stone, and (imagined) Bohemian folklore. It has been produced in collaboration with Prague-based retailer Chronoshop.cz and the historic Garnet company Granát Turnov . This collaboration combines Danish design and Czech culture, underpinned by the dark beauty of natural garnet. With just 66 pieces on offer, each one is more than limited. It’s a relic in the making. What is the dial material? Each dial incorporates hundreds of small (0.8 mm) garnets, arranged in a cluster formation, fused by a clear binding agent, and then polished down to a flat sided disc, which is overlaid by a 0.3 mm wafer of sapphire crystal treated with a red anti-reflective coating. That disc is then adhered to a gold-plated baseplate to bring out the fire of the garnet whenever it catches the light. We only use garnet — once the gemstone heart of Bohemia — from the legendary Granat Turnov surface mine. When is it available? The first batch will deliver by the end of August 2025, with subsequent batches delivered throughout the remainder of 2025. You will receive an accurate shipping estimate upon order confimation. You can buy through our site directly or via Chronoshop.cz .

watches.description: NOTE FOR CUSTOMERS IN THE USA: THIS WATCH SHIPS DDP TO THE UNITED STATES. What does this mean? As you may have heard, there’s been an “evolution” of international trade policies, which means goods entering the USA are subject to new tariffs that makes buying with confidence difficult. What we’ve decided to do is ship all of our watches to the United States Direct Duty Paid, which means the price you see online is the price you pay in total (with no hidden fees) minus any State tax that may be due (this depends on your shipping location) We hope this moveis an agreeable halfway house during these uncertain times. As always, if you have any questions or concerns, please get in touch. Pushing the Boundaries of Material Science Here at Arcanaut, we're dedicated to getting the most out of ourselves and the world around us. We don't look at materials in the same way as other brands. Almost everything is an opportunity for creativity. And thanks to our not-so-secret weapon (Black Badger), we're able to turn those opportunities into wearable art. The Havender dial is crafted from a specific layer of Scandinavian mussel shells. These shells undergo a meticulous process: they are bathed in a unique solution to strip away the outer layer, then the inner layer is finely ground using a hand drill. This results in a fine powder that is transformed into a lilac-hued composite block, ready for milling. It is then beautifully accented with white Lumicast hour markers and matching Lumicast hand tips. And the name? The Scandinavian word for ocean is "Hav". Hav + Lavender is, according to us, "Havender". Limited by nature During development, it became apparent that the Havender's creation process is far too labour-intensive to make its inclusion in the regular collection possible as planned. As such, the Havender is limited to just 33 pieces. If the model is sold out on our site, don’t forget to check in with our retailers Collective Horology in California and INDP Watches in Stockholm. All of our watches in the Composites collection are powered by Swiss-made automatic movements by Soprod (the M100), which are regulated in-house by our watchmakers in Copenhagen. watches.name: ARC II — D'Arc Roast
watches.description: What’s the story? Did you know the Danes love their coffee just as much as they do their fine watches? In fact, in the grand scheme of things, Denmark has an even more impressive record of producing world-beating baristas than it does trend-setting horologists (we’re the exception, obviously…) Four of the first seven Barista world champions were Danes, with Martin Hildebrandt, Fritz Storm, Trouls Overdahl Poulsen, and Klaus Thomsen taking home the title in years 2001, 2002, 2005, and 2006 respectively. That means Denmark is, despite not having won the title in 19 years, still the most successful nation ever to compete on the world stage. What is the dial material? This material uses specially selected beans, ground to a fine powder before being introduced to an UV-resistant binding agent and moulded into millable blocks under intense pressure. The result is definitely our tastiest (but still very much inedible) dial yet. Our steel Grand Paw hands return for the Arcanaut Arc II — D’Arc Roast Limited Edition but this time they’ve been heated until they oxidised to a warming bronze tone, which pairs beautifully with the mottled browns of the dial, and the "cream" LumiCast blocks used on the dial and hands. This inviting colourway that uses varying shades of brown alongside the muted grey of blasted stainless steel, aims to evoke the Scandinavian concept of “Hygge”, which roughly translates to, “a quality of cosiness and comfortable conviviality that engenders a feeling of contentment or well-being.” Something we feel we could all do with a little more of in our lives. On the reverse, the D’Arc Roast is fitted with one of our proprietary Glowpatch designs. A Glowpatch is a multi-component case back using three gaskets to ensure water resistance to 100 metres, a deeply engraved, Swiss Super-LumiNova filled medallion, and a sapphire crystal. This design shows an excitable coffee cup, whose name we don’t know but assume to be Joe! Orders are fulfilled in chronological order of payment confirmation.

watches.name: ARC II — Liberty Green for Collective Horology
watches.description: The story... One hundred years ago on October 15th, 1924, American president Calvin Coolidge declared the Statue of Liberty a national monument. Now, in honour of one of the world’s most recognisable symbols of freedom and in partnership with our sole US-based retailer, Collective Horology, we are releasing the Arcanaut ARC II — Liberty green model. What is the dial material? The Liberty Green is presented in our classic 40.52 mm ARC II case on a black strap. The dial is an in-house developed composite made from copper carbonate and a UV-resistant binding agent to mimic the verdigris of the statue itself. Around the outside of the CNC-machined dial are twelve LumiCast hour markers, set into the dial to provide depth, visual interest, and incredible performance when the lights get low. For this model, we have chosen the Chevron handset for maximum day- and night-time legibility. As an added quirk to this special edition model, we’ve employed a green-tinted anti-reflective coating to the underside of the sapphire crystal for an unusual but cohesive appearance. On the reverse, the Arc II — Liberty Green for Collective Horology is fitted with one of our proprietary Glowpatch case back designs, showing an anthropomorphic Flame of Liberty, streaking across the case, surrounded by stars. The Arcanaut ARC II — Liberty Green for Collective Horology is exclusively available through Collective Horology. It is limited to 100 pieces in total and is available for pre-order from today (October 15th, 2024). The first watches are expected to be ready for dispatch eight weeks from now and orders will be fulfilled in chronological order of payment confirmation. Who is it for? Most current Arcanaut owners are long-time collectors that had become jaded with mainstream brands and inauthentic sales practices. More experienced collectors tend to be less conservative with their choices and actively seek out something fresh and daring. Arcanaut satisfies those criteria by always leading from the front on the subject of design. When is it available? The new Arcanaut Arc II — Liberty Green of Collective Horology is available now. There will be a maximum of 100 pieces made and orders will be dispatched within 6–8 weeks of payment confirmation. The watches will be available exclusively via the web shop of our US retailer, Collective Horology. Learn more BUY AT COLLECTIVE HOROLOGY

watches.name: Experimental: ARC II — Tiger Sh'arc
watches.description: It was about time the case took centre stage... The Tiger Sh'Arc is something new and very different from everything we've ever done before, utilising a Zirconium Titanium composite (known as Zircuti), reminiscent of the centuries old Japanese technique called “Mokume Gane". For the first time, the case is the star of the show, but the solid silver dial and light blue PVD-coated hands are not going quietly. This tour de force is a statement for the future: nothing is out of bounds and everything — everything — is possible. The Experimental Line Concept Sometimes we have some pretty crazy ideas that take a long time to bring to life. We've decided to pursue these ambitious projects under the "Experimental" heading, because, truth be told, we're not entirely sure what we're going to discover in the process... New Materials from Arcanaut For the Tiger S'Arc we’re developing our very own Zirconium, Titanium composite created by Chad Nichols of Nichols Damascus from the United States. The material will be similar to Damascus (or Timascus) but less visually chaotic. In the initial material tests, the material’s serene striping reminded us of a Tiger Shark’s skin the second we saw it. The name fell into our laps moments later… The Tiger Sh'Arc The Tiger Sh'Arc concept is one of our premier novelties for 2024. Both this model and the Bonehead are completely original, but take the Arcanaut mantra of discovery in different directions. Our goal with the Tiger Sh'Arc is to celebrate the completely unique case form of the Arcanaut Arc II. While our focus has long been using unusual materials in new and interesting ways on dials, it would be crazy to suggest the case silhouette isn't equally as important to our brand identity. Perhaps more so. Therefore, it was time to take it on a journey of its own, and, we're happy to say, you're more than welcome to come along for the ride! Our Experimental watches for 2024 are powered by Swiss-made automatic movements by Soprod, which are regulated in-house by our watchmakers in Copenhagen. For the Bonehead, we wanted to discover what would happen when we unleashed the Badger with a series of specially created electric blue-lume discs, a batch of aerospace-grade aluminium foam, and a big tub of industrial resin. The result was so exciting that the first time James ran into Rob and Anders with a prototype in his possession, he dragged them both into the nearest men's room, locked the door, cut the lights, and presented his piece. Cue a chorus of adoring coos, showering the glowing disc with glory. Needless to say, passers-by were...perturbed. The case is unique amongst Arcanauts in that it has received a special "framing" finish, that shows off the outlines of our recognisable ARC II case silhouette. Our Experimental watches for 2024 are powered by Swiss-made automatic movements by Soprod, which are regulated in-house by our watchmakers in Copenhagen. watches.name: ARC II — Klint
watches.description: Honouring the past with a dial from the future There are few nations as well-regarded for their design prowess as Denmark. Here at Arcanaut, we take our role as custodians of Scandinavian design seriously and want to pay homage to the clean lines and cerebral elegance of iconic objects that have built our homeland's international reputation over the years. The Klint model is all about the purity of design. Using a crisp titanium dioxide composite, paired with tone-on-tone white Lumicast hour markers and a subtly redesigned "Chevron" handset, we have created our most serene model yet. We hope you like it and the bold statement it makes on the wrist. If the model is sold out on our site, don’t forget to check in with our retailers Collective Horology in California and INDP Watches in Stockholm. All of our watches in the Composites collection are powered by Swiss-made automatic movements by Soprod (M100), which are regulated in-house by our watchmakers in Copenhagen. The Klint is made in limited batches and there will just be ten pieces made in 2026. Learn more

watches.name: ARC II — D'Arc Matter Gamma Green
watches.description: Introducing the Arcanaut Arc II — D'Arc Matter Gamma Green . By feeding Scandinavian slate through an industrial coffee grinder and mixing the resulting powder with an ultra-clear UV-resistant binding agent, James Thompson, AKA The Black Badger, was able to create the D'Arc Matter composite material first seen in Arcanaut's 2021 D'Arc Matter Limited Edition release. Now, that same material returns with our new stainless steel "Grand Paw" handset (laser-cut and hand-finished in Denmark), and colourful, 3D Lumicast elements, developed by our Swiss partners RC Tritec. Housed in a 316L stainless steel case CNC-milled and assembled in Copenhagen, the Arcanaut Arc II — D'Arc Matter Gamma Green has a matte micro bead blasted finish, with brushed and hand-polished highlights applied in-house by our Danish watchmakers. The case features Arcanaut's signature "Pentablock" crown, the shape of which follows the form of the Arc case perfectly. Powered by the Swiss-made automatic Soprod M100, the Arcanaut Arc II — D'Arc Matter Gamma Green has an operating frequency of 28,800vph and a power reserve of 42 hours. The D’Arc Matter Gamma Green will only be produced in small annual batches and is available from Arcanaut directly and the brand's trusted retail partners. All of our watches in the Composites collection are powered by Swiss-made automatic movements by Soprod, which are regulated in-house by our watchmakers in Copenhagen. Learn more
